name: Rosetta Stone
note: British Museum, London.

name: Code of Hammurabi
note: The stele in the Louvre, Paris, as its sources name it: the item the Wikipedia articles sit on. Wikidata also holds the stele as an object of its own (Q12397781), with no article.

name: Dead Sea Scrolls
note: Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem, which shows a rotating selection; other fragments are in the Jordan Museum, Amman, and elsewhere.

name: Antikythera mechanism
note: National Archaeological Museum, Athens.

name: Venus de Milo
note: Louvre, Paris.

name: Ötzi
note: South Tyrol Museum of Archaeology, Bolzano.

name: Venus of Willendorf
note: Naturhistorisches Museum, Vienna.

name: Ishtar Gate
note: Pergamonmuseum, Berlin, rebuilt from the glazed bricks excavated at Babylon; counted as a find shown in a museum, not as a building standing where it was built. The museum is closed for renovation.

name: Winged Victory of Samothrace
note: Louvre, Paris.

name: Parthenon Marbles
note: British Museum, London (the Elgin Marbles, shown together in the Duveen Gallery); the rest of the frieze is in the Acropolis Museum, Athens.

name: Nebra sky disc
note: State Museum of Prehistory, Halle (Saale).

name: Laocoön and His Sons
note: Vatican Museums (Museo Pio-Clementino), Rome; found by excavation on the Esquiline in 1506.

name: Phaistos Disc
note: Heraklion Archaeological Museum, Crete.

name: Bust of Nefertiti
note: Neues Museum, Berlin.

name: Lewis chessmen
note: Split between the British Museum, London, and the National Museum of Scotland, Edinburgh.

name: Mask of Agamemnon
note: National Archaeological Museum, Athens.

name: Pergamon Altar
note: Pergamonmuseum, Berlin, rebuilt from the excavated frieze and blocks; counted as a find shown in a museum. Its wing is closed for renovation.

name: Aztec Sun Stone
note: Museo Nacional de Antropología, Mexico City.

name: Trundholm Sun Chariot
note: National Museum of Denmark, Copenhagen.

name: Royal Game of Ur
note: British Museum, London, which shows the boards from the Royal Cemetery at Ur; the item is typed both as the find and as the game.

name: Apollo Belvedere
note: Vatican Museums (Museo Pio-Clementino), Rome; a Roman marble found in the late fifteenth century.

name: Mask of Tutankhamun
note: Grand Egyptian Museum, Giza (formerly the Egyptian Museum, Cairo).

name: Riace bronzes
note: Museo Archeologico Nazionale della Magna Grecia, Reggio Calabria; the two warriors are shown together.

name: Dying Gaul
note: Capitoline Museums, Rome; found in Rome in the seventeenth century.

name: Oseberg ship
note: Museum of the Viking Age, Oslo (Bygdøy), being rebuilt.

name: Khufu ship
note: Grand Egyptian Museum, Giza.

name: Alexander Mosaic
note: Museo Archeologico Nazionale, Naples; lifted from the House of the Faun, Pompeii.

name: Standard of Ur
note: British Museum, London.

name: Augustus of Prima Porta
note: Vatican Museums (Braccio Nuovo), Rome; excavated at the Villa of Livia in 1863.

name: Charioteer of Delphi
note: Delphi Archaeological Museum.

name: Zimbabwe Birds
note: The soapstone birds from Great Zimbabwe, most of them shown together at the Great Zimbabwe site museum; the item also stands for the national emblem drawn from them.

name: Staffordshire Hoard
note: Shown in part at Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery and in part at the Potteries Museum and Art Gallery, Stoke-on-Trent.

name: Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-daro
note: National Museum, New Delhi.

name: Farnese Hercules
note: Museo Archeologico Nazionale, Naples.

name: Seated Scribe
note: Louvre, Paris.

name: Artemision Bronze
note: National Archaeological Museum, Athens.

name: Burney Relief
note: British Museum, London (the Queen of the Night relief).

name: Minoan snake goddess figurines
note: Heraklion Archaeological Museum, Crete. The item is the one the Wikipedia articles sit on, though typed as a figure of myth; the larger figurine alone has its own item (Q96751257).

name: Farnese Bull
note: Museo Archeologico Nazionale, Naples.

name: Statue of Ka-aper
note: Egyptian Museum, Cairo (the wooden statue called Sheikh el-Beled). No separate item for the statue was found; the item, typed as the man, is the one the Wikipedia articles on the statue sit on.

name: Priam's Treasure
note: Pushkin Museum, Moscow, holds most of it and the Hermitage, Saint Petersburg, a part; Berlin shows copies.

name: Barberini Faun
note: Glyptothek, Munich.

name: Dendera zodiac
note: Louvre, Paris; a ceiling relief cut from the Hathor temple at Dendera in 1821 and recovered for display, like the Parthenon Marbles.

name: Belvedere Torso
note: Vatican Museums (Museo Pio-Clementino), Rome.

name: Jockey of Artemision
note: National Archaeological Museum, Athens.

name: Boxer at Rest
note: Palazzo Massimo alle Terme (National Roman Museum), Rome.

name: Tara Brooch
note: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology, Dublin.

name: Sphinx of Naxos
note: Delphi Archaeological Museum.

name: Sword of Goujian
note: Hubei Provincial Museum, Wuhan.

name: Ram in a Thicket
note: The item covers the pair from the Royal Cemetery at Ur: one figure is in the British Museum, London, the other in the Penn Museum, Philadelphia; the sources that name a museum name the British Museum.

name: Kroisos Kouros
note: National Archaeological Museum, Athens (the Anavyssos Kouros).

name: Lord of Sipán
note: Museo Tumbas Reales de Sipán, Lambayeque, which shows the ruler's remains with the treasure of his tomb; the item is typed as the man and his mummy.

name: Mshatta Facade
note: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamonmuseum, Berlin; carved front of an Umayyad palace removed in 1903 and rebuilt in the museum, counted as the Parthenon Marbles are. The museum is closed for renovation.

name: Market Gate of Miletus
note: Pergamonmuseum, Berlin, rebuilt from the excavated gate; counted as a find shown in a museum. The museum is closed for renovation.

name: Ardagh Chalice
note: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology, Dublin.

name: Coatlicue statue
note: Museo Nacional de Antropología, Mexico City.

name: Bull-Leaping Fresco
note: Heraklion Archaeological Museum, Crete.

name: Malia bee pendant
note: Heraklion Archaeological Museum, Crete.

name: Flying Horse of Gansu
note: Gansu Provincial Museum, Lanzhou.

name: Younger Memnon
note: British Museum, London (colossal bust of Ramesses II from the Ramesseum).

name: Hoa Hakananai'a
note: British Museum, London.

name: Khafre Enthroned
note: Egyptian Museum, Cairo.

name: Berlin Gold Hat
note: Neues Museum, Berlin.

name: Houmuwu ding
note: National Museum of China, Beijing.

name: Muisca raft
note: Museo del Oro, Bogotá.

name: Bronze chariots of Qin Shi Huang
note: Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum, Xi'an, in the hall built to show them; the Terracotta Army pits themselves are a site and are not entered.

name: Menkaure triads
note: Egyptian Museum, Cairo, shows three of them together; a fourth is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

name: Harvester Vase
note: Heraklion Archaeological Museum, Crete.

name: Four-goat square zun
note: National Museum of China, Beijing.

name: Sun and Immortal Birds gold ornament
note: Jinsha Site Museum, Chengdu.

name: Lady of Cao
note: Museo Cao, El Brujo archaeological complex, La Libertad, Peru.

name: Jade mask of Pakal
note: Museo Nacional de Antropología, Mexico City.

name: Bianzhong of Marquis Yi of Zeng
note: Hubei Provincial Museum, Wuhan.

name: Throne of Tutankhamun
note: Grand Egyptian Museum, Giza.

name: Chariots of Tutankhamun
note: Grand Egyptian Museum, Giza, which shows them together.

name: Lydenburg Heads
note: The seven heads are shown together at the Iziko South African Museum, Cape Town.

name: Monolith of Tlaloc
note: Stands outside the entrance of the Museo Nacional de Antropología, Mexico City.

name: Kleobis and Biton
note: Delphi Archaeological Museum.

name: Sanxingdui bronze tree
note: Sanxingdui Museum, Guanghan.

name: Bronze Mask with Protruding Eyes
note: Sanxingdui Museum, Guanghan. The compiler's own list named the Sanxingdui bronze masks as a group; the guide that counts names this mask.

name: Sutton Hoo ship burial
note: British Museum, London (Room 41); the assemblage is entered as the group shown together, with the helmet as its best-known piece.

name: Sanxingdui bronze standing figure
note: Sanxingdui Museum, Guanghan.

name: Gold crown from the north mound of Hwangnamdaechong
note: National Museum of Korea, Seoul.

name: Colossal statue of Ramesses II
note: Grand Egyptian Museum, Giza (the atrium statue).

name: Rahotep and Nofret
note: Egyptian Museum, Cairo (the pair statue from Meidum).
